title: The transcription factor C/EBPβ promotes hyperglycemia-elicited glycolysis and liver cancer progression
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76209-9

High blood sugar in diabetes is linked to faster cancer growth, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor C/EBPβ is activated by high glucose to enhance glycolysis and HRAS-driven proliferation, promoting liver cancer progression and revealing a potential therapeutic target.

title: Longitudinal dynamics of the maternal gut virome associate with metabolic features of preterm birth
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76220-0

Here, via longitudinal multi-omics analyses, the authors show that maternal gut virome disruption precedes preterm birth and relates to metabolic alterations, with viral signatures improving preterm birth prediction, highlighting the virome as a potential target for risk assessment.

title: Antibiotic development and a path to access in India
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76186-z

India is emerging as an important developer and manufacturer of antibiotics, which includes several agents that are in clinical use or advanced stages of development. Here, the authors discuss the successes, and the implications for global access to antimicrobials.

title: Direct observation of braiding of Majorana-like zero modes in real space
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75765-4

Majorana-like zero modes are topological bound states whose exchange encodes non-trivial phase information in engineered systems. Here, the authors demonstrate boundary-localized modes in an acoustic Kekulé lattice and track their real-space evolution during braiding, revealing phase accumulation associated with their exchange.

title: Horizontally arranged covalent organic framework nanowires on poly(amidoxime) fibers for high-efficiency uranium capture
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76251-7

The efficient capture of low-concentration uranium from wastewaters is crucial for safeguarding the ecological security of water bodies. Here the authors describe an ion coordination approach to achieve controlled arrangement of covalent organic framework nanowires on the surface of poly(amidoxime) fibers providing a platform for chemical binding and photoreduction of soluble uranium into precipitates.

title: Plasma wave observations from Juno spacecraft at the Jovian bow shock
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76223-x

Plasma waves mediate conversion of solar wind kinetic energy into thermal energy at bow shocks. Here, the authors show waves at Jupiter’s bow shock resemble those at Earth but exhibit distinct harmonic structures, enhancing heating.

title: Soliton-assisted massive signal broadcasting via exceptional points
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76129-8

This study breaks the high-Q linewidth bottleneck of all-optical broadcasting using a parity-time symmetric coupled microcavity with engineered exceptional points. It achieves over 100 channel on-chip broadcasting spanning 200 nm with aggregated Terabit-per-second data rates and validates its feasibility for on-chip optical convolution computing.

title: The role of the 2’-OH group in phase separation and percolation transitions of RNA
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75961-2

By comparing RNA, DNA, and chemically modified RNA, this study demonstrates that the ribose 2′-OH group regulates nucleic acid condensation and determines the formation and material properties of RNA condensates.
